text:
# Question: generator shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut I found is: **among the red components, choose
the one with the largest axis-aligned bounding-box area; break ties by earliest
scan order.** This is stronger than “first/last/largest width/largest height”
because it fits all five usable canonical input/output pairs, including the
canonical test pair.

An exact disagreement is retained at
`repo/generators/db98b701e5bb/counterexamples/largest_bbox_area.json`. It is the
final generator's easy sample `(seed=7300, sample_index=1)`. Its three red
components, in scan order, have `(cell count, bounding-box area)` values
`(4,6)`, `(5,6)`, and `(3,4)`. The shortcut recolors the first, four-cell object;
the intended rule recolors the second, five-cell object.

I checked the intended output three ways: the task-independent Python oracle in
`workspace/reference_probe.py`, the generator's validator, and the supported
selected-authority command whose receipt is
`checks/shortcut-counterexample-final/racket.json`. The independent Python and
Racket outputs are byte-identical; the rival output differs exactly on the two
equal-area candidates.

The repaired generator emits these cases deliberately. Under default sampling,
`sample_index % 3 in {1,2}` creates an earlier size-4 and true size-5 object with
equal bounding-box area 6. Every three consecutive examples therefore contain
two such refutations. The final 100-lessons-per-band census materialized 300
lessons / 1,200 unique grids and all 1,200 query rotations with zero ambiguity
against this shortcut and the other declared rivals; see
`checks/lesson-census-v31-final.json`. This is finite named-rival evidence, not a
proof against every possible shortcut.
